calendar.note: Pleasant desert weather; avoid Thanksgiving and town event weekends.
Comfortable temperatures; avoid the New Year rush and February holiday peaks.
Dry-season hiking and volcano views; avoid major holidays.
Drier volcanic trails; Easter week 2027 falls in late March — avoid it.
Mild mountain hiking; pick clear, dark-sky Star Party dates.
Public astronomy season and forest trails; plan four days, not two.
High-country access; arrive at trailheads early.
Alpine hiking and rail before peak fall-color demand.
Aurora darkness with some hiking; storms possible.

calendarCaption: An aspirational menu, not an expectation of ten trips in thirteen months.

destinations.title: The Hidden World
destinations.weekendFitNote: Flight arrival and cave reservations decide the itinerary; move the cave tour to Saturday if needed.
destinations.flightGateway: Tucson (TUS) — usually a connection from Austin
destinations.groundTransfer: Rental car, about 1–2 hours to the area
destinations.logisticsNote: Book the cave tour before anything else; it sets the shape of the weekend.
destinations.why: A quirky historic mining town perched above one of America's carefully protected living caves — color-washed hillsides by day, a hidden world of still-growing formations underground.

hikes.name: Rotunda/Throne cave tour
hikes.caveat: A guided tour, not a wilderness hike.

hikes.name: Echo Canyon Loop, Chiricahua NM
hikes.caveat: A separate, substantial drive — not a quick add-on.

lodging.type: Historic hotel, Victorian inn or hillside casita

culture: Galleries and antiques in Old Bisbee

itinerary.plan: Fly AUS→TUS, pick up the car, drive south. Cave tour if arrival time and reservation allow; dinner in Bisbee.
Guindani Trail in the morning, Queen Mine Tour, then wander Old Bisbee.
Slow breakfast, drive back to Tucson, fly home.

cautions: Connection timing into Tucson can compress Friday.

destinations.title: The Iron Horse
destinations.weekendFitNote: Works if the train departure and return flight line up; Thursday–Sunday or Friday–Monday makes the hiking worthwhile.
destinations.flightGateway: Durango (DRO) — usually a connection from Austin
destinations.logisticsNote: The full-day rail round trip leaves no room for a substantial Saturday hike.
destinations.why: A historic narrow-gauge steam train winding through the Animas Canyon into the San Juan Mountains — the journey is the destination.

hikes.name: Andrews Lake area
hikes.caveat: Alpine scenery near Molas Pass; high elevation.

lodging.type: Historic hotel, riverside cabin or Victorian inn

culture: Silverton's historic streets during the layover

itinerary.plan: Fly AUS→DRO; short Animas River walk and dinner downtown.
Full-day train round trip to Silverton, with lunch during the layover.
Short walk, breakfast, fly home.

cautions: Verify steam vs. diesel service on your date.
Check the seasonal schedule and any track or fire restrictions.

destinations.title: The Mountain Calls
destinations.weekendFitNote: Workable with an early Friday arrival and a late Sunday flight; summer crowds and road access are the variables.
destinations.flightGateway: Seattle–Tacoma (SEA) — nonstop from Austin may be available
destinations.logisticsNote: Arrive at Paradise early on Saturday to beat weekend congestion.
destinations.why: Friday in Seattle's pop-culture orbit, Saturday on a glacier-covered volcano with wildflower meadows at its feet.

hikes.name: Skyline Trail toward Panorama Point
hikes.caveat: Optional harder alternative; longer and steeper.

culture: Tacoma Museum of Glass, if time allows

itinerary.plan: Early AUS→SEA; MoPOP for 2–3 hours; drive toward Ashford.
Early hike at Paradise, then lakes and overlooks; cabin evening.
Short walk, drive back, late flight from SEA.

cautions: Verify 2027 park entry and timed-entry rules.
Higher trails may hold snow into summer.

destinations.title: A Night Among the Stars
destinations.weekendFitNote: A long transfer both ways; three nights is better.
destinations.flightGateway: Drive ~7–8 hours from Austin, or fly to Midland (MAF)
destinations.logisticsNote: Book the Star Party before lodging, ideally near a new moon.
destinations.why: Research telescopes and some of the darkest skies in the continental U.S., in the cool high country of West Texas.

hikes.name: Skyline Drive trail segments
hikes.caveat: Depends on route — confirm before going.

lodging.type: Historic lodge, ranch cottage or adobe casita

itinerary.plan: Drive west from Austin, or fly to Midland and drive.
Mountain hike, downtime, prebooked Star Party at the observatory.
Drive or fly home.

cautions: Star Party tickets sell out; book first.

destinations.title: The Mountain Observatory
destinations.weekendFitNote: Not a satisfying Friday–Sunday trip. Plan four days minimum.
destinations.flightGateway: Montréal (YUL) — likely a connection from Austin
destinations.logisticsNote: Public tours are primarily in French; English interpretation is limited.
destinations.why: A forested Québec mountain crowned by a working astronomical observatory, at the heart of a dark-sky reserve.

hikes.name: Forest / summit-sector route
hikes.caveat: Summit climbs can have significant elevation gain — check the current Sépaq trail profile.

lodging.type: Park chalet, small auberge or rustic cabin

itinerary.plan: Fly AUS→YUL, drive to the park.
Hike, then an astronomy evening.
ASTROLab and observatory visit; explore nearby villages.
Return to Montréal and fly home.

cautions: The Popular Observatory evening is listed as returning in summer 2027 — confirm the program.

destinations.title: Islands at the End of the Road
destinations.weekendFitNote: Key West connection timing matters; flying into Miami adds 3–4 hours of driving and weakens a two-night trip.
destinations.flightGateway: Key West (EYW) — usually a connection from Austin
destinations.groundTransfer: About 45–60 minutes to Big Pine Key
destinations.logisticsNote: This is ecology and paddling, not elevation hiking.
destinations.why: Mangroves, pine rockland, tiny Key deer, wading birds and turquoise water at the far end of the Overseas Highway.

lodging.type: Waterfront cottage, island inn or state-park camping

itinerary.plan: Fly AUS→EYW, drive up to Big Pine Key.
Refuge walks, mangrove kayak, Bahia Honda.
Sunrise birding, fly home.

cautions: Don't approach or feed Key deer.

destinations.title: Into the Living Rainforest
destinations.place: Rincón de la Vieja, Costa Rica
destinations.weekendFitNote: Not a satisfying Friday–Sunday trip. Three to four nights strongly recommended.
destinations.flightGateway: Liberia (LIR) — a connection in the dry season
destinations.groundTransfer: About 45–90 minutes to the lodge zone
destinations.logisticsNote: Southwest's Austin–Liberia nonstop runs only Saturdays and Sundays, June 3 – August 2, 2027. It doesn't help a March trip or a Friday departure, and June isn't peak dry season.
destinations.why: Steaming fumaroles, bubbling mud pots, tropical birds and hot springs in the dry forest of an active volcano.

itinerary.plan: Fly AUS→LIR, transfer to the lodge.
Las Pailas circuit, birding, hot springs.
Limited morning, then the international airport buffer.

cautions: Las Pailas and Santa María sectors open on different days — verify both.
Summit and crater access has been restricted in recent years; verify before planning.

destinations.title: Under the Northern Lights
destinations.weekendFitNote: A six-day journey. Allow several evenings for aurora; it's never guaranteed.
destinations.groundTransfer: Rental car along the Ring Road
destinations.logisticsNote: An overnight flight may shift your arrival day.
destinations.why: Aurora chances above a black volcanic coast, with waterfalls, basalt columns and outlet glaciers by day.

hikes.name: Glacier walk
hikes.caveat: Requires a professional guide and suitable conditions.

lodging.type: Countryside cottage, farm guesthouse or cabin

itinerary.plan: Fly AUS→KEF via a hub.
Reykjavík and a geothermal soak.
South Coast waterfalls and a short hike.
Black-sand beach and glacier-area trails.
Flexible weather day and an aurora attempt.
Return.

cautions: Early October storms and short days are real constraints.
Never plan around a guaranteed aurora.

destinations.title: The Lake of Volcanoes
destinations.weekendFitNote: A five-to-six-day journey; the road transfer alone can take 3–4+ hours.
destinations.groundTransfer: Road transfer to the lake, often 3–4+ hours
destinations.logisticsNote: The January–February dry season usually brings clearer volcano views.
destinations.why: A vast lake ringed by volcanoes and Maya communities, paired with the colonial streets of Antigua.

lodging.type: Eco-lodge, boat-access inn or courtyard hotel

itinerary.plan: Fly AUS→GUA; transfer to Antigua or the lake depending on arrival.
Lake villages, one guided hike, one relaxation or boat day.
Antigua culture and cafés.
Return.

cautions: Don't take unescorted remote village-to-village trails without checking current local conditions.

destinations.title: Somewhere Beyond the Horizon
destinations.weekendFitNote: A six-day journey; if flights are inefficient, six nights may be materially better.
destinations.flightGateway: Ponta Delgada (PDL) via the U.S. East Coast or Lisbon
destinations.logisticsNote: November is a scheduling preference, not a weather claim: cooler, wetter and windier, with shorter days and fewer crowds.
destinations.why: Green volcanic crater lakes, drifting mist, thermal water and Atlantic cliffs in the middle of the ocean.

hikes.name: Vista do Rei → Sete Cidades
hikes.caveat: Arrange transport back from the end.

hikes.name: Short scenic walks
hikes.caveat: For days when rain or wind makes ridgelines unpleasant.

lodging.type: Stone cottage, rural eco-lodge, thermal hotel or guesthouse

itinerary.plan: International transit AUS→PDL; an overnight routing may consume a day.
Sete Cidades if the weather clears.
Serra Devassa and Lagoa do Fogo.
Furnas lake hike and a thermal bath.
Island culture and flexible rain-day plans.
Return.

cautions: Verify trail closures before setting out.
Crater views aren't promised; keep the itinerary weather-flexible.
